fact: The luminous heart of Perseus, leading a scattered cluster of young stars.
bio: Mirfak (Alpha Persei) is a yellow-white supergiant roughly 510 light-years away, the brightest star in Perseus. It is the leading light of the Alpha Persei Cluster, a loose group of hot young stars sharing its motion through space.
cultural: The name comes from the Arabic for 'the elbow'. In the classical figure Perseus holds the head of Medusa — near the winking demon-star Algol — and Mirfak marks the hero's side.
